extracted.intended_audience: humanities researchers, research evaluators, university administrators, funders, librarians and scholarly-society staff involved in designing or using evaluation metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and implementing humanities research-evaluation indicators that are grounded in discipline-relevant values and practices rather than transplanted quantitative proxies. Guidance covers identifying values, mapping values→practices→outputs, community engagement, data and technical constraints, and example indicators (openness, equity, quality, collegiality, accessibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse-engineer metrics from practices and values
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation metrics should be developed by reverse engineering from the scholarly practices and core values (what funders, institutions, societies and individuals want to encourage), not by imposing off-the-shelf metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by articulating the values you want to reward, brainstorm the related practices and resulting outputs, then derive indicators that approximate progress toward those values. The article emphasizes doing this as the central approach of HuMetricsHSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate and use core values to drive indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit values (examples: collegiality, openness, equity, quality, community) as the basis for creating evaluation frameworks and indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify locally relevant values through discussion; use them as lenses when assessing practices (e.g. ask how 'equity' informs syllabus design). Values lists will vary by institution and should be debated, not assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map values → practices → outputs (values-mapping exercise)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any scholarly practice (e.g. creating a syllabus), identify related practices, the resulting persistent objects (outputs), and which values drive those practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exercises (like Table 1 in the article) to list related practices, outputs (syllabus, bibliography, code of conduct), and possible driving values (quality, diversity, accessibility, openness). This mapping informs appropriate indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and measure diverse scholarly practices beyond traditional outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation should capture the full range of humanities work—teaching, open educational materials, mentoring, organizing events, public engagement—not just monographs and articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include indicators that acknowledge pedagogy, service, outreach, and other non-traditional scholarly labor in promotion, tenure or assessment portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include digital and public humanities outputs and develop assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Create ways to evaluate digital/public humanities projects (multimodal OA pedagogical materials, digitization, data visualizations, collaborative digital scholarship) that often lack clear citable objects and conventional metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify citable components, document contributions and roles, and develop qualitative and quantitative approaches to capture impact and labor (e.g. data on reuse, downloads, documented contributions). Refer to discipline-specific guidelines (MLA, AHA, AAA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure appropriate credit and attribution for collaborative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment must account for collaborative projects where credit is distributed and behind-the-scenes labor may not be visible through traditional metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design indicators or documentation practices that surface contributors' roles; clarify what counts as the citable object in loosely bounded digital projects and how to attribute credit fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer community engagement and consensus-building in metric development
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric design should be driven by inclusive, deliberative processes (workshops, debates) that allow diverse stakeholders to voice values and build trust and buy-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold bottom-up workshops across roles (faculty, librarians, graduate students, administrators) to debate and refine values and indicators; the process itself is important for legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid top-down, administrator-imposed or 'representative democracy' frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose evaluation frameworks without genuine, open participation — such imposition undermines trust and adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure discussions are organic and participatory; avoid closed working groups that claim representativeness but exclude key voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow localized remixing and adaptation of frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that one-size-fits-all lists of values/metrics are unrealistic; provide frameworks designed for local adaptation to institutional and disciplinary contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide templates and processes that units can adapt; emphasize that institutional/personal goals should determine final metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor formative over summative assessment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use assessment approaches that support reflection and growth rather than simply judging faculty against fixed benchmarks and penalizing failure to meet them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design metrics and evaluation workflows that surface development opportunities and narrative evidence, not only binary pass/fail indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simplistic single-proxy metrics (e.g. 'impact' as sole measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not treat single proxies like citation counts or an ROI-style impact metric as adequate representations of value; such measures can commodify scholarship and skew behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rich, contextualized evidence and multiple indicators tied to articulated values to reduce perverse incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure organizational transparency and data-correction rights for faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty should have visibility into the data used to judge them and the ability to correct or contest it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make metrics, underlying data sources and calculations transparent and allow faculty to review and amend records used in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address and mitigate data limitations and coverage gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the dearth of machine-readable, permissively-licensed data and limited coverage of humanities outputs in popular citation indices; metrics must account for these limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek alternative data sources, improve local data collection (e.g. institutional repositories, syllabi archives), or develop technical solutions (scraping where appropriate) while respecting legal/ethical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use indicators aligned to specific values (examples: openness, equity, quality, accessibility, collegiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive concrete indicators that approximate the institution's chosen values—e.g. number of items in institutional repository as openness, diversity of students mentored as equity, citations/awards as one facet of quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what each indicator is intended to capture and its limitations; combine quantitative proxies with qualitative narratives or documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure openness through concrete signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize 'openness' via indicators such as deposits to institutional repositories, use of open licenses, and publication of open-source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track OA deposits, licensing metadata, and public availability of materials; pair these signals with documentation of intent and reuse where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure equity through diversity and inclusion indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess equity by tracking diversity in mentorship, workshop participation, authorship and curricular choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recruitment and participation data, mentorship records, and syllabus content analyses (e.g. diversity of authors included) as evidence toward equity goals, taking care with privacy and ethical uses of demographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure accessibility as part of values-based evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include accessibility (e.g. syllabi formatted for screen readers, inclusive course materials) among evaluation criteria to reflect commitments to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for accessible formats, alternative text, readable structure and licensing that permits redistribution; include documentation in portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat 'quality' as multi-dimensional and not reducible to citations alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use citations and awards as one set of signals of quality, but complement them with evidence of rigor, originality and disciplinary significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask qualitative questions (e.g. 'Does the syllabus include creative and/or rigorous assignments?') and include peer review statements, external assessments, or narrative justification alongside quantitative data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for disciplinary differences in citation, collaboration and regional orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Design metrics that acknowledge humanities-specific citation patterns, lower coverage in major indexes, and different collaboration norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust expectations and benchmarks by discipline and region; avoid importing STEM evaluation standards uncritically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating perverse incentives that commodify scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Guard against metric designs that encourage quantity-over-quality behaviors or commodification of knowledge (neoliberal ROI thinking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test proposed indicators for likely behavioral side-effects; prioritize indicators that reward desired practices rather than superficially boosting numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make methods, tools and code for metrics development open and transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: When developing computational tools or indicators, publish methods and code openly to embody the values of openness and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HuMetricsHSS publishes about its work and uses technologists to write open-source code; replicate by documenting algorithms, data sources, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design indicators mindful of practical data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing computational indicators or tools, ensure the required data are realistically available (e.g. syllabi at scale, student learning data, traces of online discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before committing to automated tools, audit available data, licensing and technical barriers; where data are missing, consider alternative qualitative evidence or institutional data collection improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use workshops and iterative community testing to refine values and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Test value lists and candidate indicators in iterative, cross-role workshops to surface disagreements and refine indicators through dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HuMetricsHSS team ran multiple workshops; even when consensus wasn't reached on a single list, the discussion process itself advanced institutional readiness and clarified trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage narrative/intentionality statements in evaluation portfolios
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow scholars to explain the intentionality behind their work (how values shaped choices) as part of evaluation evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage faculty to document why they designed syllabi or projects a certain way, linking practice to values to provide context for quantitative signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be innovative and pragmatic about technical solutions to data gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Where canonical datasets lack coverage, explore technical innovations (e.g. scraping, local repositories) while considering ethics and sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine technical approaches with policy and cultural change (e.g. encourage permissive licensing and repository deposit) rather than relying solely on risky scraping strategies.
